## [1.4.0-dev.1](https://github.com/TahmidSummy/proxy-patches/compare/v1.3.2...v1.4.0-dev.1) (2026-11-07)

### ✨ New features

* **Choose which browser opens your links.** With Morphe's **Open links externally** turned on, Reddit sends links to your phone's default browser. You can now pick a different one, for example Firefox when Chrome is your default, without changing the default for the rest of your phone.
  * **Where:** long-press the app icon → **Proxy settings** → **Browser for external links** (below the username and password).
  * **The list** shows every browser installed on your phone. **System default** puts it back to normal.
  * **Saving:** it's saved as soon as you pick, with no need to tap Save.
  * **Coverage:** it works for links in posts and comments, and for link posts opened from the feed or the post page.
  * **If you uninstall the browser** you picked, links go back to your default browser, and the setting tells you it's missing.

### ⚠️ After updating

* **The browser you pick doesn't use this app's proxy.** Pages opened in any browser go over that browser's own connection, as before. If you want those pages on a proxy too, pick a browser that has its own proxy set up.
* **Nothing changes until you pick a browser.** Morphe's **Open links externally** (in Morphe's settings inside Reddit) still decides whether links leave Reddit at all. This setting only chooses where they go.
* **Without Morphe's Open links externally:** if that patch isn't in your app, the setting says so and has no effect.

### ✅ Tested

Tested with Reddit 2026.40.0 on an Android 15 emulator, with a test browser installed next to Chrome (Chrome being the default):

* **The way you patch it:**
  * the original Reddit 2026.40.0 from APKMirror;
  * Morphe's official patches (v2.1.0) and Proxy Patches applied together in one run;
  * all 31 checks passed. The same tests also passed with Proxy added on its own to an already Morphe-patched Reddit.
* **Browser for external links:**
  * nothing picked → Chrome, as before;
  * test browser picked → the link opens there, from the feed and from the post page;
  * picked browser uninstalled → back to Chrome, and the setting shows it's missing;
  * back to System default → Chrome.
* **Everything else**, unchanged and rechecked:
  * no traffic going around the proxy on HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 (including real test proxies), a fresh install, and switching Wi-Fi ⇄ mobile;
  * the proxy-problem messages;
  * Run without proxy, the long-press shortcut, the write-only password, and blocked screenshots.
